rules: "Red Line" is the game title: never translate or transliterate it.
Tone: sober, precise, modern military command terminal. Short imperative labels, no exclamation marks unless the source has one, no emojis.

Keep weapon system names and designations exactly as written (M1A2 Abrams, T-90M, S-400, F-35A, Rafale, HIMARS, Shahed-136…), as well as acronyms like ORBAT, SIGINT, HUMINT, IMINT, OSINT, AESA, EW, DEFCON, ICBM, SLBM, MIRV, R&D when the target language normally uses them.
Keep units and symbols: km, m, kg, h, min, s, %, $, Mach, kn (knots may be localized). Monetary amounts are always US dollars.
Keyboard keys (Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Esc, Enter, Space, Tab) may be localized as on that language's keyboards; single letters stay as is.

Address the player with the polite/formal form where the language distinguishes (Sie, usted, Вы, siz, Anda, आप, 您 used sparingly); Japanese: concise です/ます style or noun phrases for labels; Korean: 합니다 style or noun phrases.
Real country and city names: use the standard exonym of the target language.

Variables like {{name}} must be kept exactly (same spelling, never translated); you may move them to fit the grammar. In dispatch templates {{A}} and {{B}} are country names, {{P}} a place name, {{X}} and {{Y}} values given in the source context.

French grammatical variants of a country variable ({{nationLe}}, {{NationLe}}, {{deNation}}, {{aNation}}, {{aLe}}, {{bDe}}…) all simply mean the country name in other languages: keep each such variable that appears in the source, used as the plain country name.
Keep line breaks (\n) and punctuation structure; keep leading/trailing symbols such as ›, —, ·, /, \\ .
Abbreviated source labels (ending with a dot, like "Rens." or "Diplo.") must stay very short in the target language.
Game clock prefix "J+" (jour) becomes the local day prefix (English "D+").
French number units "k", "M", "Md" (milliard) become the local short scale (English k, M, B).
